analysis: Examined the scoped stop-string change. EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift head 14-32 adds an optional CBv2StopStringScope. When a scope is set, the reported matched sequence is recomputed via the SDK StopHoldback, so it matches only inside the scope. Per the docs, GPT-OSS limits the scope to the Harmony final message. The function returns nil when the scan did not stop. Otherwise it returns the first candidate that is a prefix of the tail after the scan's emitted text. EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift head 249-250 passes the same stopStringScope into the CBv2Request, so the engine stop and the reported sequence use one scope. This is consistent, and no plaintext or crypto path changes. With the scope, analysis text cannot trigger a stop, which reduces the chance of hidden reasoning ending a request early. Remaining questions for the next pass: (1) how stopStringScope is derived (ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope) and whether it can only come from the verified model type, never from a request field; (2) whether scan.text is the emitted visible text, so the tail offset is correct. A wrong offset would only misreport the finish metadata and would not expose data. The docs in inference.md (head 2424-2961) are mostly unchanged context; the only changed row is 1846, which describes the GPT-OSS scope. The submodule bumps change libs/mlx (31f550a->72dffa2), libs/mlx-swift (4926d3d->c633d22) and libs/mlx-swift-lm (aee6ebb->25bcd63). Their contents are not supplied. They may touch StopHoldback/CBv2StopStringScope, kernels (TB-007), media decode, the prefix cache (T-041) or MTP. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety, so the submodule diffs need separate review. Relevant threats: TB-007/T-028 (in-process inference) and T-008 (fail-closed encryption of output is unaffected). There is no visible change to attestation, keys, billing or the cache.
